who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), write-only lane on the check's stack
where: crates/blaze-cli/src/engine_check.rs `checking` and its drive closure; tests/engine_body_reads_memory_tests.rs a_changed_archive_checksum_enters_the_body_through_the_graph
what: the archive test overflowed the 2 MiB test stack (2,109,888 bytes, 109 frames). `checking` was one 523 KB frame and its drive closure 172 KB: at O0 every local, `?` temporary and struct literal of a 1,500-line function gets its own slot for the whole call, so the stack held every stage's temporaries at once. Boxing header slots one at a time did not fix it.
cost: two passes: one boxing round that moved the number, then the stage split
cause: a command written as one function: every stage's temporaries summed in one frame, live under every callee
whys: nothing states the stack a check needs; nothing fails when a frame grows; the one-worker path runs the bodies inline on that same stack
class: a frame that sums its stages: any long function holding stage temporaries for its whole call, under deep callees
prevention: stages are #[inline(never)] functions over one Drive state allocated once in the command's frame (drive, one_phase, run_stage, bodies_phase, heads_phase, put_phase, lines_of, print_answer); a const size assert on Drive; test a_whole_check_fits_its_stated_stack on a 1 MiB thread; proposed: clippy large_stack_frames deny at 64 KiB
annoyance: frame sizes are known only from a backtrace with frame addresses; the write-only lane cannot measure size_of::<CliError>() or a frame
workaround: read frame sizes off the overflow backtrace's stack pointers
